issues.description: Class identifier mismatch: the exercise expects a class named 'Meal' (problem statement and UML reference the Meal class; the solution repository provides src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java) but the template repository does not contain a Meal implementation. Instead the template contains an 'Order' class with the same fields and methods as the expected Meal. This naming inconsistency (missing Meal class and presence of Order) will cause compilation failures or test mismatches because code, tests and the UML refer to Meal while the template exposes Order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template match the problem statement and solution by providing a Meal class in the template. Either (A) add src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java implementing the same constructor and getters as the solution's Meal, or (B) if Order was intended, rename template Order.java to Meal.java and update any references (e.g., Main and tests) so the class name is Meal. Ensure the Meal class has a constructor Meal(String, String[]) and getName()/getIngredients() getters to match the solution and UML.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution describe and use a domain entity named 'Meal' (class Meal with constructor Meal(String, String[]) and getters). The template repository instead provides an 'Order' class (Order(String, String[]), getName(), getIngredients()) and leaves Meal.java empty, and Main in the template refers to Order. This mismatch means the same core concept (a named dish with an array of ingredient names) is referred to as 'Meal' in the problem statement and solution but as 'Order' in the template. Students will be confused mapping requirements (which mention Meal and SealSaloon methods that accept Meal) to the starter code (which defines Order and no Meal), potentially blocking implementation or causing incorrect renames.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the entity name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the template's Order class and its file to Meal (class Meal with the same constructor and getters) and update all template references (e.g., Main) to use Meal, or (B) populate the template's Meal.java with the same implementation as the solution's Meal and remove or merge the Order class so the template uses Meal everywhere. Ensure constructor/signature and usages match the problem statement (Meal) and solution.
